task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md (full) and judge.toml (header + criteria grep, 5 likert criteria)
evidence: All three scored dimensions (mode = "batched", aggregation = "weighted_mean") carry explicit per-criterion independence and continue-after-failure wording; the two gates use aggregation = "all_pass" and are exempt. (1) task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:13: 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature'; line 7 adds 'give that criterion its lowest score ..., state what you observed, and move on.' (2) task/tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:12: 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; line 7 'move on'; line 18 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' (3) task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:12: 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.'; line 14 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row.' No scored prompt, judge.toml criterion or app_context.md line tells the judge to stop at the first failure (grep for stop/halt/abort/first fail/skip the rest found none in task tests). The only cross-row zeroing is the restated global browser gate (functional:13, polish:12, visual:12), which is the intended in-dimension gate (check 29), not a sibling-failure cascade. Criterion descriptions in functional/judge.toml each name their own control and own failure condition (e.g. hro_undo_full:128 'the other successful undos in this review are the control'; hro_stale_refused:200) rather than depending on another criterion's verdict. Template comparison: the frozen template's scored prompts carry the same rule (functional:68 'Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'); the task rewrites the wording but preserves the semantics. Adversarial reasoning: (a) broken app that could pass — an app with a single broken early feature (e.g. job opening validation) cannot drag other rows to zero because the prompt mandates re-setup on a new job and forbids using sibling verdicts; conversely it cannot gain credit, since setup 'never earns credit for the feature that failed'. (b) conforming app that could fail — an app whose live board update works but whose polish note preservation is fine would not be zeroed by an unrelated functional failure; the only intrinsic precondition is polish hro_pol_live_board (judge.toml:23 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds, preservation cannot be shown and this row is 0'), which is the row's own observable precondition (a non-live app genuinely cannot demonstrate preserved state during an update) and the brief requires live updates; this is a correlated-precondition question for checks 39/40, not an independence-wording defect here. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json states full configured grading is absent, so actual judge adherence to the wording is NOT EXERCISED; the row is a source-wording check, which the frozen bytes directly establish. The private check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed; wording was applied manually per deterministic-checks.md:54.
